title: Courage Passed From Teacher to Student
overview: Paul, writing from prison, encourages his young coworker Timothy to stay brave, hold on to the teaching he received, and not be ashamed of Paul's chains.

parts.label: A letter to a spiritual son (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: Paul writes as someone sent by God to speak for Jesus, and calls Timothy his dear son because he likely brought him to faith and trained him. The letter comes from prison and has long been read as one of Paul's last.

parts.label: Tears, prayers, family faith (vv. 3-5)
parts.note: Paul says he serves the same God his Jewish ancestors served, so he sees his faith as continuing theirs, not abandoning it. Timothy's father was Greek, but his Jewish mother Eunice and grandmother Lois passed their faith on to him.

parts.label: Rekindle the gift, don't fear (vv. 6-8)
parts.note: Placing hands on someone was a ceremony of prayer that sent them into a task, and Paul tells Timothy to revive the gift he received then, like blowing on embers. Being linked to a prisoner was shameful and risky, so Paul urges him not to pull away but to share the hardship.

parts.label: Grace planned before time (vv. 9-12)
parts.note: Paul sums up his message: God rescues people out of his own kindness, not their track record, and this has now come to light in Jesus, who broke death's power. Paul trusts God to keep safe what he has placed in God's care until the final day, though scholars are unsure whether that means his own life or the message he was given.

parts.label: Guard what was handed over (vv. 13-14)
parts.note: Paul pictures his teaching as valuables left in someone's safekeeping. Timothy is to hold it unchanged, relying on the Holy Spirit, God's presence living in believers.

parts.label: Deserted, yet not alone (vv. 15-18)
parts.note: Asia here is a Roman province in what is now western Turkey, and many believers there turned away from Paul, including two men known only from this mention. Onesiphorus, by contrast, searched Rome until he found him, and Paul's prayer for his household leads some to think he had died, though the text does not say.

think: Who has stood by you when it cost them something, and what did that mean to you?
